Al-Bukhari and Muslim transmitted from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "While three men—in one narration, from among those before you—were walking, rain overtook them, so they took refuge in a cave in a mountain, and a rock from the mountain fell over the mouth of the cave and sealed it upon them. Some of them said to others: 'Consider the deeds you have done sincerely for God, so that perhaps He will relieve you of this through them.'" The hadith is given in full, and it is well known; its fame makes its completion unnecessary.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When he said in the belly of the fish, "There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers," the fish cast him out. It is also said: "among those who glorify" means among those who prayed in the belly of the fish. I say: The more apparent view is that it is the glorification of the tongue accompanied by the heart, and this is indicated by the hadith of Abu Hurayrah mentioned before, which al-Tabari recorded: "He glorified in the belly of the fish. The angels heard his glorification and said: 'Our Lord, we hear a faint sound in a strange land.'" On this view, "was" (kana) is supplementary (za'idah), meaning: "had he not been among those who glorify." In the book of Abu Dawud, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "The invocation of Dhu al-Nun in the belly of the fish: 'There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers'—no Muslim man ever supplicates with it for anything except that it is answered for him." Yunus, peace be upon him, was earlier one who prayed and glorified, and in the belly of the fish likewise. In the report: the fish was addressed: "We did not make Yunus a provision for you; We made you a refuge and a place of worship for him." This has been mentioned before.

**Issue 1: The first verse, ﴿And indeed Yunus was among the messengers﴾**

Yunus is Dhu al-Nun, and he is the son of Matta (Ibn Matta). He was the son of the old woman with whom Ilyas (Elijah) stayed. Ilyas hid with her from his people for six months, while Yunus was still an infant nursing. Yunus's mother served him herself, kept him company, and withheld no honour from him that she was able to give. Then Ilyas grew weary of the narrowness of houses and went off to the mountains. The woman's son Yunus died, so she set out in search of Ilyas, following his trail through the mountains until she found him. She asked him to pray to Allah for her, that perhaps He would restore her son to life. Ilyas came to the child fourteen days after his death, performed ablution, prayed, and supplicated Allah. Allah brought Yunus ibn Matta back to life through the supplication of Ilyas, peace be upon him.

Allah sent Yunus to the people of Nineveh (Ninawa), in the land of Mosul. They had been worshipping idols, but then they repented, as has been explained earlier in the commentary on Surat Yunus [[vol. 8, p. 384, first or second edition.]]. The story of Yunus in his departure in anger has already been mentioned in Surat al-Anbiya' [[vol. 11, p. 329 onward, first or second edition.]].

Scholars differed over whether his prophethood (risalah) came before the whale swallowed him or after. Al-Tabari reported, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, that Jibril (peace be upon him) came to Yunus and said: "Go to the people of Nineveh and warn them that the punishment has come close to them." He said: "Let me find a mount." He said: "The matter is more urgent than that." He said: "Let me find sandals." He said: "The matter is more urgent than that." So he became angry, went to the ship, and boarded it. When he boarded the ship, the ship stopped; it neither advanced nor retreated. He said: "So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon him. Then the whale came, wagging its tail, and it was called out to the whale: 'O whale! We did not make you a provision for Yunus; rather, We made you a refuge and a place of worship for him.'" He said: "So the whale swallowed him from that place, and carried him until it passed by al-Ubulla, then carried him until it passed by the Tigris, then carried on until it cast him up at Nineveh."

Al-Harith narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, saying: Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: "The prophethood of Yunus came only after the whale spat him out."

Those who held this view argued that a messenger does not depart in anger from his Lord, so what happened from him occurred before prophethood.

Others said: this occurred from him after he had called the people to whom he was sent to what Allah had commanded him to call them to, and after he had conveyed to them the message of his Lord. But he promised them the coming of the punishment with which he had warned them, at a time that he had set for them. He then left them when they did not repent and did not return to obedience to Allah. When the punishment overshadowed the people and enveloped them, as Allah the Exalted said in His revelation, they repented to Allah, and Allah removed the punishment from them. The news reached Yunus that they were safe and that the punishment he had promised them had been lifted. He became angry at this and said: "I promised them a promise, and they made my promise a lie." So he went off, angry at his Lord, and disliked returning to them, since they had been found to lie against him. This was narrated by Sa'id ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas. This has already been mentioned in al-Anbiya', and it is the sound view, as will come under the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾ [al-Saffat: 147].

The name Yunus is not declined (it does not take nunation), because it is a foreign (non-Arabic) name. Even if it were Arabic, it would be declined, though the yā' at its beginning would have been a case in point, since there is no pattern yuf'ul among verbs. Likewise, if you name someone Ya'far (as an Arabic name), you decline it, but if you name someone Ya'far in a way that makes it fixed, you do not decline it. [[This is because the resemblance to the verb has been removed from it, unlike Ya'far, which is on the pattern of yaqtul, and so is not declined.]]

**Issue 2: The Exalted's words, ﴿when he ran away﴾**

Al-Mubarrad said: the root meaning of abaqa is "to go far away," and from it comes ghulam abiq (a runaway slave). Others said: Yunus was called "runaway" only because he left without the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, hiding himself from the people.

﴿to the laden ship﴾, that is, the filled ship. The word fulk (ship) may be masculine or feminine, singular or plural, as has been mentioned earlier [[see vol. 2, p. 194, second edition.]].

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim said: He was called a runaway because he ran away from servitude. Servitude is only the abandonment of desire and the giving of oneself up when Allah's affairs are at stake. When he did not give up himself when the resolve of the king was strongly upon him, as has been explained earlier in al-Anbiya', and preferred his own desire, the name "runaway" stuck to him. The resolve of the king was for the sake of Allah's command, not for his own affair, and for the portion of Allah's right, not for his own portion. Yunus strove, but did not hit upon the correct course that was with Allah, so he was called a runaway and one who had blame (mulīm).

**Issue 3: The Exalted's words, ﴿so he cast lots﴾**

Al-Mubarrad said: fa-qara'a (he drew lots). He said: its root is from the arrows (sihām) that are shuffled. ﴿and he was among the losers﴾.

He said: "among the defeated." The reciters said: "his argument was refuted (dahadat hujjatuhu), and Allah refuted it (adhdahahā Allah)." Its origin is from slipping. A poet said:

*We have slain the defeated ones on every path,*
*and the eyes have been cooled by their slaughter.*

That is, "the defeated ones."

**Issue 4: The Exalted's words, ﴿Then the whale swallowed him, and he was blameworthy﴾**

That is, he did what he deserved blame for. A mulūm is one who is blamed, whether he deserved it or not. It is said: mulīm is one who is faulted (ma'īb). It is said: lām al-rajul when he did something and became faulted for that deed.

﴿Had he not been among those who glorify (Allah)﴾. Al-Kisa'i said: "anna" was not made kasra because of the entry of the lām, since the lām does not belong to it. Al-Nahhas said: The matter is as he said; the lām is in the answer of lawlā (if not).

﴿Had he not been among those who glorify (Allah), he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are raised﴾, that is, among those who pray. It means as a punishment for him, that is, the belly of the whale would be his grave until the Day of Resurrection.

Scholars differed over how long he remained in the belly of the whale. Al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: forty days. Al-Dahhak said: twenty days. Ata said: seven days. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: three days. It was also said: one hour. And Allah knows best.

**Issue 5:** Al-Tabari narrated from a hadith of Abu Hurayra who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, willed to imprison Yunus in the belly of the whale, He revealed to the whale: 'Take him, but do not tear his flesh nor break his bone.' So it took him and then plunged with him to its dwelling place in the sea. When it reached the bottom of the sea, Yunus heard a sound and said to himself, 'What is this?' Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to him, while he was in the belly of the whale: 'This is the glorification of the creatures of the sea.'" He said: "So he glorified (Allah) while in the belly of the whale." He said: "The angels heard his glorification and said: 'Our Lord, we hear a weak voice in a strange land.'" He said: "That is My servant Yunus, who disobeyed Me, so I imprisoned him in the belly of the whale in the sea." They said: "The righteous servant whose righteous deed ascended to You every day and night?" He said: "Yes." So they interceded for him at that point, and He commanded the whale to cast him out onto the shore, as He said: ﴿And he was sick﴾. His sickness that Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, described was that the whale cast him on the shore like a newborn child, with flesh and bone exposed.

It has also been narrated that the whale travelled with the ship, lifting its head, and Yunus breathed through it and glorified (Allah), and it did not leave them until they reached the land. It then spat him out safe, with nothing changed in him, and so they became Muslims. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned this in his tafsir [a commentary on the Qur'an].

Ibn al-'Arabi said: More than one of our companions informed me, on the authority of Imam al-Haramayn Abu al-Ma'ali 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni, that he was asked whether the Creator is in a direction. He said: "No; He is exalted above that." He was asked: "What is the evidence for that?" He said: "The evidence is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Do not prefer me over Yunus ibn Matta.'" He was asked: "What is the argument from this report?" He said: "I will not say it until this guest of mine takes a thousand dinars to pay off a debt." Two men stood up and said: "It is upon us." He said: "He should not depend on two, because that would be a burden for him." One man said: "It is upon me." He then said: "Yunus ibn Matta threw himself into the sea, and the whale swallowed him, so he ended up at the bottom of the sea in three darknesses, and he called out ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I was among the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87], as Allah reported about him. Muhammad (ﷺ), when he sat upon the green carpet and was lifted up to heights until he reached a place where he could hear the scratching of the pens, and his Lord conversed with him with what He conversed with him, and revealed to him what He revealed, was not closer to Allah, the Exalted, than Yunus was in the belly of the whale in the darkness of the sea."

**Issue 6:** Al-Tabari mentioned that when Yunus (peace be upon him) boarded the ship, a violent wind struck its people. They said: "This is because of the sin of one of you." Yunus said, knowing that he himself was the one with the sin: "This is my sin, so throw me into the sea." They refused him until they cast their arrows, ﴿so he drew lots and was among the losers﴾. He said to them: "I have already told you that this matter is because of my sin." They refused him until they cast their arrows a second time, and he was among the losers. They refused to throw him into the sea until they repeated their arrows a third time, and he was among the losers. When he saw that, he cast himself into the sea, and that was under the night, so the whale swallowed him.

It is also narrated that when he boarded the ship, he lay down and slept. They sailed not far when a wind came upon them that nearly sank the ship. The people of the ship gathered and called out: "Wake up the sleeping man, he should pray with us." So he prayed to Allah with them, and Allah removed that wind from them. Then Yunus went back to his place and slept. Another wind came that nearly sank the ship, so they woke him and called upon Allah, and the wind lifted. He said: "While they were like that, a huge whale raised its head toward them, wanting to swallow the ship. Yunus said to them: 'O people! This is because of me. If you threw me into the sea, you would sail on, and the wind and the terror would leave you.' They said: 'We will not throw you until we cast lots; whoever the lot falls upon, we will throw him into the sea.' He said: 'So they cast lots, and it fell on Yunus.' He said to them: 'O people, throw me, for because of me you have been afflicted.' They said: 'We will not do it until we cast lots once more.' They did, and it fell on Yunus. He said to them: 'O people, throw me, for because of me you have been afflicted.' That is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿so he cast lots and was among the losers﴾."

That is, the arrow fell on him. So they took him to the front of the ship to throw him into the sea, and suddenly the fish was there with its mouth open. Then they brought him to the side of the ship, and there was the fish. Then they turned back to the other side, and the fish was there with its mouth open. When he saw that, he threw himself down, and the fish swallowed him. Then God Most High revealed to the fish: "I did not make him your provision, but I made your belly a vessel for him." So he remained in the belly of the fish for forty nights, and he called out in the darkness: "There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers." ﴿So We answered him and delivered him from distress, and thus do We deliver the believers.﴾ This has been mentioned before and will come again.

In this there is a point of jurisprudence: casting lots (qur'ah, drawing lots by chance) was practised in the law of those before us (shar' man qablana, the revealed law of earlier communities), and it came into our law as has been mentioned before in Surat Al 'Imran [see vol. 4, p. 86, first or second edition]. Ibn al-'Arabi said: The casting of lots appears in the law in three situations. The first: when the Prophet (ﷺ) intended to travel, he would draw lots among his wives, and whichever lot came out, he took her with him. The second: it was reported to the Prophet (ﷺ) that a man had freed six slaves, having no other property, so he drew lots among them, freed two and kept four in bondage. The third: two men brought a dispute to him concerning inheritances that had become obscure, and he said: "Go and seek the truth, cast lots, and let each of you absolve the other." These are three situations, namely the division in marriage, in manumission, and in partition, and the operation of lots in them is to remove ambiguity and cut off the disease of arbitrary preference.

Our scholars differed about drawing lots among wives when going on military campaign, in two opinions. The sound one of them is drawing lots, and this is the view of the jurists of the regions (fuqaha' al-amsar). That is because travelling with all of them is impossible, and choosing one of them over the others is preference, so nothing remains but the lot. Likewise in the matter of the slaves, the Sunnah applies, for each of the two was a third, which is the amount in which one may free slaves during terminal illness, and specifying the two by personal desire is not permitted by the sharia, so nothing remains but the lot. Likewise, when disputes arise over the specific items of inheritance and nothing distinguishes the right except the lot, it becomes the basis for specifying the entitled party when it is unclear. He said: In my view the truth is that it should be applied in every ambiguous matter, for that is clearer for it, stronger for settling the ruling in it, and more evident for removing the ambiguity from it. For this reason we say that drawing lots among wives in divorce is like drawing lots among slave-women in manumission.

Seventh: casting lots to throw a human being into the sea is not permitted. That occurred in the time of Yunus only as a preliminary to confirming his proof and increasing his faith. It is not permissible to kill a person who is disobedient, nor to throw him into fire or the sea. Rather, the prescribed punishments (hudud) and discretionary punishments (ta'zir) are applied to him according to the measure of his offence. Some people have thought that when the sea becomes rough upon a people and they are compelled to lighten the ship, lots are drawn among them and some are thrown overboard to lighten it. This is corrupt, for the ship is not lightened by throwing off some men; rather, it is goods that are lightened. Instead, they should be patient with the decree of God, Mighty and Majestic.

Eighth: God Most High informed us that Yunus was among those who glorified (al-musabbihin), and that his glorification was the cause of his deliverance. For this reason it is said: good deeds raise their doer when he stumbles. Ibn 'Abbas said: "among those who glorify" means among those who prayed obediently before the disobedience. Wahb said: among the worshippers. Al-Hasan said: He had no prayer in the belly of the fish, but he had put forward a good deed in a time of ease, so God reminded him of it in a time of trial. They said: "The righteous servant whose righteous deed ascended to You every day and night?" He said: "Yes." His sickness that Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, described was that the whale cast him on the shore like a newborn child, with flesh and bone exposed.

It has also been narrated that the whale travelled with the ship, lifting its head, and Yunus breathed through it and glorified (Allah), and it did not leave them until they reached the land. It then spat him out safe, with nothing changed in him, and so they became Muslims. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned this in his tafsir [a commentary on the Qur'an].

Ibn al-'Arabi said: More than one of our companions informed me, on the authority of Imam al-Haramayn Abu al-Ma'ali 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni, that he was asked whether the Creator is in a direction. He said: "No; He is exalted above that." He was asked: "What is the evidence for that?" He said: "The evidence is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Do not prefer me over Yunus ibn Matta.'" He was asked: "What is the argument from this report?" He said: "I will not say it until this guest of mine takes a thousand dinars to pay off a debt." Two men stood up and said: "It is upon us." He said: "He should not depend on two, because that would be a burden for him." One man said: "It is upon me." He then said: "Yunus ibn Matta threw himself into the sea, and the whale swallowed him, so he ended up at the bottom of the sea in three darknesses, and he called out ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I was among the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87], as Allah reported about him. Muhammad (ﷺ), when he sat upon the green carpet and was lifted up to heights until he reached a place where he could hear the scratching of the pens, and his Lord conversed with him with what He conversed with him, and revealed to him what He revealed, was not closer to Allah, the Exalted, than Yunus was in the belly of the whale in the darkness of the sea."

**Issue 6:** Al-Tabari mentioned that when Yunus (peace be upon him) boarded the ship, a violent wind struck its people. They said: "This is because of the sin of one of you." Yunus said, knowing that he himself was the one with the sin: "This is my sin, so throw me into the sea." They refused him until they cast their arrows, ﴿so he drew lots and was among the losers﴾. He said to them: "I have already told you that this matter is because of my sin." They refused him until they cast their arrows a second time, and he was among the losers. They refused to throw him into the sea until they repeated their arrows a third time, and he was among the losers. When he saw that, he cast himself into the sea, and that was under the night, so the whale swallowed him.

It is also narrated that when he boarded the ship, he lay down and slept. They sailed not far when a wind came upon them that nearly sank the ship. The people of the ship gathered and called out: "Wake up the sleeping man, he should pray with us." So he prayed to Allah with them, and Allah removed that wind from them. Then Yunus went back to his place and slept. Another wind came that nearly sank the ship, so they woke him and called upon Allah, and the wind lifted. He said: "While they were like that, a huge whale raised its head toward them, wanting to swallow the ship. Yunus said to them: 'O people! This is because of me. If you threw me into the sea, you would sail on, and the wind and the terror would leave you.' They said: 'We will not throw you until we cast lots; whoever the lot falls upon, we will throw him into the sea.' He said: 'So they cast lots, and it fell on Yunus.' He said to them: 'O people, throw me, for because of me you have been afflicted.' They said: 'We will not do it until we cast lots once more.' They did, and it fell on Yunus. He said to them: 'O people, throw me, for because of me you have been afflicted.' That is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿so he cast lots and was among the losers﴾."

That is, the arrow fell on him. So they took him to the front of the ship to throw him into the sea, and suddenly the fish was there with its mouth open. Then they brought him to the side of the ship, and there was the fish. Then they turned back to the other side, and the fish was there with its mouth open. When he saw that, he threw himself down, and the fish swallowed him. Then God Most High revealed to the fish: "I did not make him your provision, but I made your belly a vessel for him." So he remained in the belly of the fish for forty nights, and he called out in the darkness: "There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers." ﴿So We answered him and delivered him from distress, and thus do We deliver the believers.﴾ This has been mentioned before and will come again.

In this there is a point of jurisprudence: casting lots (qur'ah, drawing lots by chance) was practised in the law of those before us (shar' man qablana, the revealed law of earlier communities), and it came into our law as has been mentioned before in Surat Al 'Imran [see vol. 4, p. 86, first or second edition]. Ibn al-'Arabi said: The casting of lots appears in the law in three situations. The first: when the Prophet (ﷺ) intended to travel, he would draw lots among his wives, and whichever lot came out, he took her with him. The second: it was reported to the Prophet (ﷺ) that a man had freed six slaves, having no other property, so he drew lots among them, freed two and kept four in bondage. The third: two men brought a dispute to him concerning inheritances that had become obscure, and he said: "Go and seek the truth, cast lots, and let each of you absolve the other." These are three situations, namely the division in marriage, in manumission, and in partition, and the operation of lots in them is to remove ambiguity and cut off the disease of arbitrary preference.

Our scholars differed about drawing lots among wives when going on military campaign, in two opinions. The sound one of them is drawing lots, and this is the view of the jurists of the regions (fuqaha' al-amsar). That is because travelling with all of them is impossible, and choosing one of them over the others is preference, so nothing remains but the lot. Likewise in the matter of the slaves, the Sunnah applies, for each of the two was a third, which is the amount in which one may free slaves during terminal illness, and specifying the two by personal desire is not permitted by the sharia, so nothing remains but the lot. Likewise, when disputes arise over the specific items of inheritance and nothing distinguishes the right except the lot, it becomes the basis for specifying the entitled party when it is unclear. He said: In my view the truth is that it should be applied in every ambiguous matter, for that is clearer for it, stronger for settling the ruling in it, and more evident for removing the ambiguity from it. For this reason we say that drawing lots among wives in divorce is like drawing lots among slave-women in manumission.

Seventh: casting lots to throw a human being into the sea is not permitted. That occurred in the time of Yunus only as a preliminary to confirming his proof and increasing his faith. It is not permissible to kill a person who is disobedient, nor to throw him into fire or the sea. Rather, the prescribed punishments (hudud) and discretionary punishments (ta'zir) are applied to him according to the measure of his offence. Some people have thought that when the sea becomes rough upon a people and they are compelled to lighten the ship, lots are drawn among them and some are thrown overboard to lighten it. This is corrupt, for the ship is not lightened by throwing off some men; rather, it is goods that are lightened. Instead, they should be patient with the decree of God, Mighty and Majestic.

Eighth: God Most High informed us that Yunus was among those who glorified (al-musabbihin), and that his glorification was the cause of his deliverance. For this reason it is said: good deeds raise their doer when he stumbles. Ibn 'Abbas said: "among those who glorify" means among those who prayed obediently before the disobedience. Wahb said: among the worshippers. Al-Hasan said: He had no prayer in the belly of the fish, but he had put forward a good deed in a time of ease, so God reminded him of it in a time of trial. Indeed a good deed raises its doer, and when he stumbles he finds a support.

I say: From this meaning is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever among you is able to have a hidden good deed (khabi'ah min 'amal salih), let him do so." So he strives in worship and is eager for one trait of his good deeds, which he makes sincere between himself and his Lord, stores for the day of his need and poverty, hides with his effort, and conceals from his creation, so that its benefit reaches him when he is most in need of it. Al-Bukhari and Muslim transmitted from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "While three men—in one narration, from among those before you—were walking, rain overtook them, so they took refuge in a cave in a mountain, and a rock from the mountain fell over the mouth of the cave and sealed it upon them. Some of them said to others: 'Consider the deeds you have done sincerely for God, so that perhaps He will relieve you of this through them.'" The hadith is given in full, and it is well known; its fame makes its completion unnecessary.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When he said in the belly of the fish, "There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers," the fish cast him out. It is also said: "among those who glorify" means among those who prayed in the belly of the fish. I say: The more apparent view is that it is the glorification of the tongue accompanied by the heart, and this is indicated by the hadith of Abu Hurayrah mentioned before, which al-Tabari recorded: "He glorified in the belly of the fish. The angels heard his glorification and said: 'Our Lord, we hear a faint sound in a strange land.'" On this view, "was" (kana) is supplementary (za'idah), meaning: "had he not been among those who glorify." In the book of Abu Dawud, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "The invocation of Dhu al-Nun in the belly of the fish: 'There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers'—no Muslim man ever supplicates with it for anything except that it is answered for him." This has passed in Surat al-Anbiya' [see vol. 11, p. 329 and following, first or second edition]. Yunus, peace be upon him, was earlier one who prayed and glorified, and in the belly of the fish likewise. In the report: the fish was addressed: "We did not make Yunus a provision for you; We made you a refuge and a place of worship for him." This has been mentioned before.

**Issue 1: The first verse, ﴿And indeed Yunus was among the messengers﴾**

Yunus is Dhu al-Nun, and he is the son of Matta (Ibn Matta). He was the son of the old woman with whom Ilyas (Elijah) stayed. Ilyas hid with her from his people for six months, while Yunus was still an infant nursing. Yunus's mother served him herself, kept him company, and withheld no honour from him that she was able to give. Then Ilyas grew weary of the narrowness of houses and went off to the mountains. The woman's son Yunus died, so she set out in search of Ilyas, following his trail through the mountains until she found him. She asked him to pray to Allah for her, that perhaps He would restore her son to life. Ilyas came to the child fourteen days after his death, performed ablution, prayed, and supplicated Allah. Allah brought Yunus ibn Matta back to life through the supplication of Ilyas, peace be upon him.

Allah sent Yunus to the people of Nineveh (Ninawa), in the land of Mosul. They had been worshipping idols, but then they repented, as has been explained earlier in the commentary on Surat Yunus [[vol. 8, p. 384, first or second edition.]]. The story of Yunus in his departure in anger has already been mentioned in Surat al-Anbiya' [[vol. 11, p. 329 onward, first or second edition.]].

Scholars differed over whether his prophethood (risalah) came before the whale swallowed him or after. Al-Tabari reported, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, that Jibril (peace be upon him) came to Yunus and said: "Go to the people of Nineveh and warn them that the punishment has come close to them." He said: "Let me find a mount." He said: "The matter is more urgent than that." He said: "Let me find sandals." He said: "The matter is more urgent than that." So he became angry, went to the ship, and boarded it. When he boarded the ship, the ship stopped; it neither advanced nor retreated. He said: "So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon him. Then the whale came, wagging its tail, and it was called out to the whale: 'O whale! We did not make you a provision for Yunus; rather, We made you a refuge and a place of worship for him.'" He said: "So the whale swallowed him from that place, and carried him until it passed by al-Ubulla, then carried him until it passed by the Tigris, then carried on until it cast him up at Nineveh."

Al-Harith narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, saying: Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: "The prophethood of Yunus came only after the whale spat him out."

Those who held this view argued that a messenger does not depart in anger from his Lord, so what happened from him occurred before prophethood.

Others said: this occurred from him after he had called the people to whom he was sent to what Allah had commanded him to call them to, and after he had conveyed to them the message of his Lord. But he promised them the coming of the punishment with which he had warned them, at a time that he had set for them. He then left them when they did not repent and did not return to obedience to Allah. When the punishment overshadowed the people and enveloped them, as Allah the Exalted said in His revelation, they repented to Allah, and Allah removed the punishment from them. The news reached Yunus that they were safe and that the punishment he had promised them had been lifted. He became angry at this and said: "I promised them a promise, and they made my promise a lie." So he went off, angry at his Lord, and disliked returning to them, since they had been found to lie against him. This was narrated by Sa'id ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas. This has already been mentioned in al-Anbiya', and it is the sound view, as will come under the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾ [al-Saffat: 147].

The name Yunus is not declined (it does not take nunation), because it is a foreign (non-Arabic) name. Even if it were Arabic, it would be declined, though the yā' at its beginning would have been a case in point, since there is no pattern yuf'ul among verbs. Likewise, if you name someone Ya'far (as an Arabic name), you decline it, but if you name someone Ya'far in a way that makes it fixed, you do not decline it. [[This is because the resemblance to the verb has been removed from it, unlike Ya'far, which is on the pattern of yaqtul, and so is not declined.]]

**Issue 2: The Exalted's words, ﴿when he ran away﴾**

Al-Mubarrad said: the root meaning of abaqa is "to go far away," and from it comes ghulam abiq (a runaway slave). Others said: Yunus was called "runaway" only because he left without the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, hiding himself from the people.

﴿to the laden ship﴾, that is, the filled ship. The word fulk (ship) may be masculine or feminine, singular or plural, as has been mentioned earlier [[see vol. 2, p. 194, second edition.]].

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim said: He was called a runaway because he ran away from servitude. Servitude is only the abandonment of desire and the giving of oneself up when Allah's affairs are at stake. When he did not give up himself when the resolve of the king was strongly upon him, as has been explained earlier in al-Anbiya', and preferred his own desire, the name "runaway" stuck to him. The resolve of the king was for the sake of Allah's command, not for his own affair, and for the portion of Allah's right, not for his own portion. Yunus strove, but did not hit upon the correct course that was with Allah, so he was called a runaway and one who had blame (mulīm).

**Issue 3: The Exalted's words, ﴿so he cast lots﴾**

Al-Mubarrad said: fa-qara'a (he drew lots). He said: its root is from the arrows (sihām) that are shuffled. ﴿and he was among the losers﴾.

He said: "among the defeated." The reciters said: "his argument was refuted (dahadat hujjatuhu), and Allah refuted it (adhdahahā Allah)." Its origin is from slipping. A poet said:

*We have slain the defeated ones on every path,*
*and the eyes have been cooled by their slaughter.*

That is, "the defeated ones."

**Issue 4: The Exalted's words, ﴿Then the whale swallowed him, and he was blameworthy﴾**

That is, he did what he deserved blame for. A mulūm is one who is blamed, whether he deserved it or not. It is said: mulīm is one who is faulted (ma'īb). It is said: lām al-rajul when he did something and became faulted for that deed.

﴿Had he not been among those who glorify (Allah)﴾. Al-Kisa'i said: "anna" was not made kasra because of the entry of the lām, since the lām does not belong to it. Al-Nahhas said: The matter is as he said; the lām is in the answer of lawlā (if not).

﴿Had he not been among those who glorify (Allah), he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are raised﴾, that is, among those who pray. It means as a punishment for him, that is, the belly of the whale would be his grave until the Day of Resurrection.

Scholars differed over how long he remained in the belly of the whale. Al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: forty days. Al-Dahhak said: twenty days. Ata said: seven days. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: three days. It was also said: one hour. And Allah knows best.

**Issue 5:** Al-Tabari narrated from a hadith of Abu Hurayra who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, willed to imprison Yunus in the belly of the whale, He revealed to the whale: 'Take him, but do not tear his flesh nor break his bone.' So it took him and then plunged with him to its dwelling place in the sea. When it reached the bottom of the sea, Yunus heard a sound and said to himself, 'What is this?' Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to him, while he was in the belly of the whale: 'This is the glorification of the creatures of the sea.'" He said: "So he glorified (Allah) while in the belly of the whale." He said: "The angels heard his glorification and said: 'Our Lord, we hear a weak voice in a strange land.'" He said: "That is My servant Yunus, who disobeyed Me, so I imprisoned him in the belly of the whale in the sea." They said: "The righteous servant whose righteous deed ascended to You every day and night?" He said: "Yes." So they interceded for him at that point, and He commanded the whale to cast him out onto the shore, as He said: ﴿And he was sick﴾. His sickness that Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, described was that the whale cast him on the shore like a newborn child, with flesh and bone exposed.

It has also been narrated that the whale travelled with the ship, lifting its head, and Yunus breathed through it and glorified (Allah), and it did not leave them until they reached the land. It then spat him out safe, with nothing changed in him, and so they became Muslims. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned this in his tafsir [a commentary on the Qur'an].

Ibn al-'Arabi said: More than one of our companions informed me, on the authority of Imam al-Haramayn Abu al-Ma'ali 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni, that he was asked whether the Creator is in a direction. He said: "No; He is exalted above that." He was asked: "What is the evidence for that?" He said: "The evidence is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Do not prefer me over Yunus ibn Matta.'" He was asked: "What is the argument from this report?" He said: "I will not say it until this guest of mine takes a thousand dinars to pay off a debt." Two men stood up and said: "It is upon us." He said: "He should not depend on two, because that would be a burden for him." One man said: "It is upon me." He then said: "Yunus ibn Matta threw himself into the sea, and the whale swallowed him, so he ended up at the bottom of the sea in three darknesses, and he called out ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I was among the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87], as Allah reported about him. Muhammad (ﷺ), when he sat upon the green carpet and was lifted up to heights until he reached a place where he could hear the scratching of the pens, and his Lord conversed with him with what He conversed with him, and revealed to him what He revealed, was not closer to Allah, the Exalted, than Yunus was in the belly of the whale in the darkness of the sea."

**Issue 6:** Al-Tabari mentioned that when Yunus (peace be upon him) boarded the ship, a violent wind struck its people. They said: "This is because of the sin of one of you." Yunus said, knowing that he himself was the one with the sin: "This is my sin, so throw me into the sea." They refused him until they cast their arrows, ﴿so he drew lots and was among the losers﴾. He said to them: "I have already told you that this matter is because of my sin." They refused him until they cast their arrows a second time, and he was among the losers. They refused to throw him into the sea until they repeated their arrows a third time, and he was among the losers. When he saw that, he cast himself into the sea, and that was under the night, so the whale swallowed him.

It is also narrated that when he boarded the ship, he lay down and slept. They sailed not far when a wind came upon them that nearly sank the ship. The people of the ship gathered and called out: "Wake up the sleeping man, he should pray with us." So he prayed to Allah with them, and Allah removed that wind from them. Then Yunus went back to his place and slept. Another wind came that nearly sank the ship, so they woke him and called upon Allah, and the wind lifted. He said: "While they were like that, a huge whale raised its head toward them, wanting to swallow the ship. Yunus said to them: 'O people! This is because of me. If you threw me into the sea, you would sail on, and the wind and the terror would leave you.' They said: 'We will not throw you until we cast lots; whoever the lot falls upon, we will throw him into the sea.' He said: 'So they cast lots, and it fell on Yunus.' He said to them: 'O people, throw me, for because of me you have been afflicted.' They said: 'We will not do it until we cast lots once more.' They did, and it fell on Yunus. He said to them: 'O people, throw me, for because of me you have been afflicted.' That is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿so he cast lots and was among the losers﴾."

That is, the arrow fell on him. So they took him to the front of the ship to throw him into the sea, and suddenly the fish was there with its mouth open. Then they brought him to the side of the ship, and there was the fish. Then they turned back to the other side, and the fish was there with its mouth open. When he saw that, he threw himself down, and the fish swallowed him. Then God Most High revealed to the fish: "I did not make him your provision, but I made your belly a vessel for him." So he remained in the belly of the fish for forty nights, and he called out in the darkness: "There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers." ﴿So We answered him and delivered him from distress, and thus do We deliver the believers.﴾ This has been mentioned before and will come again.

In this there is a point of jurisprudence: casting lots (qur'ah, drawing lots by chance) was practised in the law of those before us (shar' man qablana, the revealed law of earlier communities), and it came into our law as has been mentioned before in Surat Al 'Imran [see vol. 4, p. 86, first or second edition]. Ibn al-'Arabi said: The casting of lots appears in the law in three situations. The first: when the Prophet (ﷺ) intended to travel, he would draw lots among his wives, and whichever lot came out, he took her with him. The second: it was reported to the Prophet (ﷺ) that a man had freed six slaves, having no other property, so he drew lots among them, freed two and kept four in bondage. The third: two men brought a dispute to him concerning inheritances that had become obscure, and he said: "Go and seek the truth, cast lots, and let each of you absolve the other." These are three situations, namely the division in marriage, in manumission, and in partition, and the operation of lots in them is to remove ambiguity and cut off the disease of arbitrary preference.

Our scholars differed about drawing lots among wives when going on military campaign, in two opinions. The sound one of them is drawing lots, and this is the view of the jurists of the regions (fuqaha' al-amsar). That is because travelling with all of them is impossible, and choosing one of them over the others is preference, so nothing remains but the lot. Likewise in the matter of the slaves, the Sunnah applies, for each of the two was a third, which is the amount in which one may free slaves during terminal illness, and specifying the two by personal desire is not permitted by the sharia, so nothing remains but the lot. Likewise, when disputes arise over the specific items of inheritance and nothing distinguishes the right except the lot, it becomes the basis for specifying the entitled party when it is unclear. He said: In my view the truth is that it should be applied in every ambiguous matter, for that is clearer for it, stronger for settling the ruling in it, and more evident for removing the ambiguity from it. For this reason we say that drawing lots among wives in divorce is like drawing lots among slave-women in manumission.

Seventh: casting lots to throw a human being into the sea is not permitted. That occurred in the time of Yunus only as a preliminary to confirming his proof and increasing his faith. It is not permissible to kill a person who is disobedient, nor to throw him into fire or the sea. Rather, the prescribed punishments (hudud) and discretionary punishments (ta'zir) are applied to him according to the measure of his offence. Some people have thought that when the sea becomes rough upon a people and they are compelled to lighten the ship, lots are drawn among them and some are thrown overboard to lighten it. This is corrupt, for the ship is not lightened by throwing off some men; rather, it is goods that are lightened. Instead, they should be patient with the decree of God, Mighty and Majestic.

Eighth: God Most High informed us that Yunus was among those who glorified (al-musabbihin), and that his glorification was the cause of his deliverance. For this reason it is said: good deeds raise their doer when he stumbles. Ibn 'Abbas said: "among those who glorify" means among those who prayed obediently before the disobedience. Wahb said: among the worshippers. Al-Hasan said: He had no prayer in the belly of the fish, but he had put forward a good deed in a time of ease, so God reminded him of it in a time of trial. Indeed a good deed raises its doer, and when he stumbles he finds a support.

I say: From this meaning is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever among you is able to have a hidden good deed (khabi'ah min 'amal salih), let him do so." So he strives in worship and is eager for one trait of his good deeds, which he makes sincere between himself and his Lord, stores for the day of his need and poverty, hides with his effort, and conceals from his creation, so that its benefit reaches him when he is most in need of it. Al-Bukhari and Muslim transmitted from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "While three men—in one narration, from among those before you—were walking, rain overtook them, so they took refuge in a cave in a mountain, and a rock from the mountain fell over the mouth of the cave and sealed it upon them. Some of them said to others: 'Consider the deeds you have done sincerely for God, so that perhaps He will relieve you of this through them.'" The hadith is given in full, and it is well known; its fame makes its completion unnecessary.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When he said in the belly of the fish, "There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers," the fish cast him out. It is also said: "among those who glorify" means among those who prayed in the belly of the fish. I say: The more apparent view is that it is the glorification of the tongue accompanied by the heart, and this is indicated by the hadith of Abu Hurayrah mentioned before, which al-Tabari recorded: "He glorified in the belly of the fish. The angels heard his glorification and said: 'Our Lord, we hear a faint sound in a strange land.'" On this view, "was" (kana) is supplementary (za'idah), meaning: "had he not been among those who glorify." In the book of Abu Dawud, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "The invocation of Dhu al-Nun in the belly of the fish: 'There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers'—no Muslim man ever supplicates with it for anything except that it is answered for him." This has passed in Surat al-Anbiya' [see vol. 11, p. 329 and following, first or second edition]. Yunus, peace be upon him, was earlier one who prayed and glorified, and in the belly of the fish likewise. In the report: the fish was addressed: "We did not make Yunus a provision for you; We made you a refuge and a place of worship for him." This has been mentioned before.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 37, verses 145–148 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So We cast him onto the open shore while he was ailing. And We caused to grow over him a gourd plant.﴾ It is narrated that the fish threw him up on the shore of a town in Mosul. Ibn Qusayt said, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: "Yunus was cast out in the open, and Allah caused a gourd plant (yaqtin) to grow over him." We said: "O Abu Hurayrah, what is the yaqtinah?" He said: "It is the gourd plant (shajarat al-dubba'). Allah prepared for him a wild doe (aruwwiyyah) [[al-Aruwwiyyah: the female of the wild goats (wu'ul).]] which ate from the tender plants of the earth, or its soft plants, and she would spread her legs (tafshij) [[Tafshij: she would part her legs.]] over him and nurse him with her milk every evening and morning until he grew strong."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The fish carried him until it expelled him on the shore of the sea, and it cast him out like a newborn child, nothing of his creation having been diminished."

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, chose him and made him among the righteous. Then He commanded him to go to his people and inform them that Allah the Exalted had accepted their repentance. So he set out toward them until he met a shepherd and asked him about the people of Yunus, and about their condition and how they were. The shepherd informed him that they were well and that they were hopeful that their messenger would return to them. He said to him: "Then inform them that I have met Yunus." He said: "And what (sign)?" He said: "This place where you are standing will bear witness for you that you met Yunus." He said: "And what (sign)?" He said: "This tree will bear witness for you that you met Yunus." The shepherd returned to his people and informed them that he had met Yunus, but they denied him and intended harm against him. He said: "Do not hasten against me until morning." When morning came, he went with them to the place where he had met Yunus, and he questioned it, and it informed them that he had met Yunus. He also questioned the sheep and the tree, and they informed them that he had met Yunus. Then Yunus came to them after that.

Al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned this report and what precedes it.

Al-Akhfash said: "In the open ground (al-fada')." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "The wide part of the earth." Al-Farra' said: "Al-'ara' is the empty place." He said: Abu 'Ubaydah said: "Al-'ara' is the surface of the earth," and he cited a man from Khuza'ah:

"I raised a leg whose stumbling I do not fear, and I cast off my garments in the open land."

Al-Akhfash, regarding His words "wa-huwa saqim" (while he was ailing), reported the plural of saqim as saqma, saqama and siqam. [[The addition is from I'rab al-Quran of al-Nahhas, being his report from al-Akhfash.]]

He said in this surah: "fa-nabadhnahu bil-'ara'," and in Surat Nun wal-Qalam [al-Qalam: 1]: ﴿Had not a blessing from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast out on the open shore while he was blameworthy﴾ [al-Qalam: 49]. The answer is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, here informs that He cast him onto the open shore while he was not blameworthy, and that had it not been for the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, he would have been cast onto the open shore while he was blameworthy. This was stated by al-Nahhas.

As for His words "wa-anbatna 'alayhi shajaratan min yaqtin" (And We caused to grow over him a gourd plant): "'alayhi" here means "'indahu" (near him), like His words: ﴿And they have a sin against me﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 14], meaning "'indi" (with me). In a report: "The gourd and the watermelon are from Paradise," and we have mentioned it in the book al-Tadhkirah. Al-Mubarrad said: Every plant that has no stalk, whose leaves spread upon the ground, is called yaqtinah, like the gourd, the watermelon and the colocynth. If it has a stalk that carries it, it is simply a tree (shajarah). If it stands upright by roots that spread, it is a najmah, whose plural is najm. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the star and the tree prostrate﴾ [al-Rahman: 6]. A similar statement is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and Muqatil. They said: Every plant that extends and spreads over the ground, not standing erect, and has no stalk, like the cucumber, the watermelon, the pumpkin and the colocynth, is a yaqtin. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It is everything that grows and then dies in the same year, and this includes the banana. I say: The banana has a stalk. Al-Jawhari said: Al-yaqtin is that which has no stalk, like the gourd plant and the like. It was said to him: "O Yunus, you who did not create, did not water, and did not cause to grow, do you grieve over a small bush? I am the One who created a hundred thousand people or more, and you want me to uproot them in a single hour, though they have repented and I have accepted their repentance. Then where is My mercy, O Yunus? I am the Most Merciful of the merciful."

Anas said: A broth containing gourd and dried meat was served to the Prophet ﷺ, and he began to follow the gourd around the dish. Anas said: "I have not ceased to love gourd from that day." The imams recorded it.

So they separated every mother from her child, went out, cried to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and sought forgiveness. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, withheld the punishment from them. Yunus, peace be upon him, went out in the morning awaiting the punishment, but he saw nothing; and whoever lies and has no proof is killed. So Yunus went out in anger, and came to a people in a ship, and they carried him and recognized him. When he entered the ship, the ship stopped while the other ships were moving right and left. They said: 'What is wrong with your ship?' They said: 'We do not know.' Yunus, peace be upon him, said: 'In it there is a slave who has fled from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and it will not move until you cast him out.' They said: 'As for you, O Prophet of Allah, we will not cast you out.' He said: 'Then cast lots, and whoever is chosen, let him fall.' They cast lots, and the lot fell upon Yunus, but they refused to leave him. He said: 'Cast lots three times, and whoever is chosen, let him fall.' They cast lots, and the lot fell upon Yunus three times, or he said three times, and he fell. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had appointed a fish for him, which swallowed him while he was descending with it toward the bottom of the earth. Yunus, peace be upon him, heard the glorification of the pebbles, and ﴿he called out in the darkness: There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87]." He said: "The darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the belly of the fish." He said: "So We cast him onto the open shore while he was ailing," [and] he said: "like the condition of a featherless chick that has been plucked. He said: "The Messenger of Allah, Yunus, went out and found a boy tending sheep. He said: 'O boy, who are you?' He said: 'From the people of Yunus.' He said: 'When you come to them, inform them that you have met Yunus.' He said: 'If you are Yunus, I know that whoever lies is killed when he has no proof; so who will bear witness for me?' He said: 'This tree and this place.' He said: 'Then command them.' So Yunus said to them: 'When this boy comes to you, bear witness for him.' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'The boy returned to his people, and he had a protected position, and he had brothers. He came to the king and said: "I have met Yunus, and he sends you greetings." He ordered that he be killed. They said: "He has proof, so send someone with him." He came to the tree and the place and said to them: "I adjure you by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, do you bear witness that I met Yunus?" They said: "Yes!" He said: The people returned in alarm, saying to him: "The tree and the earth have borne witness for him," and they came to the king and informed him of what they had seen.' 'Abd Allah said: 'The king took the boy's hand, seated him in his place, and said: "You are more worthy of this place than I am." 'Abd Allah said: 'That boy then governed their affairs for forty years.'" Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas said: "It has become clear in this hadith that Yunus had been sent before the fish swallowed him, by this chain which is not to be taken by analogy. There is also in it the benefit that the people of Yunus believed and repented before they saw the punishment, for in it he informed them that the punishment would come to them within three days, so they separated every mother from her child, and they cried out with one cry to Allah, Mighty and Majestic." Some scholars said: They saw the signs of the punishment and repented. This does not prevent it, and what the scholars have said on this has already been mentioned in Surat Yunus [[See vol. 8, p. 384, first or second edition.]], so let it be consulted there.

His words: ﴿or they increase﴾. The meanings of "aw" in His words "aw ashaddu qaswah" have already passed in al-Baqarah [[See vol. 1, pp. 463 ff., second or third edition.]]. Al-Farra' said: "Aw" here means "bal" (rather). Others said: It means "wa" (and), and from this is the poet's saying:

"When the matter of war grew intense among us, and we considered the winds, or the clouds (rizam)."

Meaning: "or [they were] more", and this is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the matter of the Hour is but as a glance of the eye or closer﴾ [16:77]. Ja'far ibn Muhammad read "ila mi'at alf wa-yazidun" without hamza, so "yazidun" is in the place of nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning "and they are increasing." Al-Nahhas said: These two opinions are not sound according to the Basrans. They rejected that "aw" (or) means "bal" (rather) or means "wa" (and), because "bal" is for turning away from the first statement and affirming what follows it, and exalted is Allah, mighty and majestic, above that; or [it is for] moving from one thing to another, and this is not the place for that. The meaning of "wa" is different from the meaning of "aw," so if either of them meant the other, the meanings would be nullified. And if that were permissible, it would be [more concise to say] "wa-arsalnahu ila akthara min mi'atay alf" (and We sent him to more than two hundred thousand).

Al-Mubarrad said: The meaning is "and We sent him to a group which, if you saw them, you would say: they are a hundred thousand or more," and the servants were addressed in terms of what they know. It was said: It is like when you say: "Zayd or 'Amr came to me," while you know which of the two came to you, except that you have made it ambiguous to the addressee. Al-Akhfash and al-Zajjaj said: That is, "or they increase in your estimation."

Ibn 'Abbas said: They exceeded one hundred thousand by twenty thousand. Ubayy ibn Ka'b narrated it as a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ) report. And also from Ibn 'Abbas: thirty thousand. Al-Hasan and al-Rabi': some thirty thousand. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: seventy thousand.

﴿So they believed, and We gave them enjoyment for a time﴾ — that is, until the end of their appointed terms.

He said: "And what (sign)?" He said: "This place where you are standing will bear witness for you that you met Yunus." He said: "And what (sign)?" This was stated by al-Nahhas.

So Yunus went out in anger, and came to a people in a ship, and they carried him and recognized him. When he entered the ship, the ship stopped while the other ships were moving right and left. They said: 'What is wrong with your ship?' They said: 'We do not know.' Yunus, peace be upon him, said: 'In it there is a slave who has fled from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and it will not move until you cast him out.' They said: 'As for you, O Prophet of Allah, we will not cast you out.' He said: 'Then cast lots, and whoever is chosen, let him fall.' They cast lots, and the lot fell upon Yunus, but they refused to leave him. He said: 'Cast lots three times, and whoever is chosen, let him fall.' They cast lots, and the lot fell upon Yunus three times, or he said three times, and he fell. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had appointed a fish for him, which swallowed him while he was descending with it toward the bottom of the earth. Yunus, peace be upon him, heard the glorification of the pebbles, and ﴿he called out in the darkness: There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87]." He said: "The darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the belly of the fish." He said: "So We cast him onto the open shore while he was ailing," [and] he said: "like the condition of a featherless chick that has been plucked. He said: 'This tree and this place.' He said: 'Then command them.' So Yunus said to them: 'When this boy comes to you, bear witness for him.' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'The boy returned to his people, and he had a protected position, and he had brothers. He came to the king and said: "I have met Yunus, and he sends you greetings." He ordered that he be killed. They said: "He has proof, so send someone with him." He came to the tree and the place and said to them: "I adjure you by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, do you bear witness that I met Yunus?" They said: "Yes!" He said: The people returned in alarm, saying to him: "The tree and the earth have borne witness for him," and they came to the king and informed him of what they had seen.' Some scholars said: They saw the signs of the punishment and repented. This does not prevent it, and what the scholars have said on this has already been mentioned in Surat Yunus [[See vol. 8, p. 384, first or second edition.]], so let it be consulted there.

His words: ﴿or they increase﴾. The meanings of "aw" in His words "aw ashaddu qaswah" have already passed in al-Baqarah [[See vol. 1, pp. 463 ff., second or third edition.]]. Al-Farra' said: "Aw" here means "bal" (rather). Others said: It means "wa" (and), and from this is the poet's saying:

It was said: It is like when you say: "Zayd or 'Amr came to me," while you know which of the two came to you, except that you have made it ambiguous to the addressee. This is the sound view on the matter, and that the ruling of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, concerning them was not like His ruling concerning others, in the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might﴾ [Ghafir: 85], and His words, Mighty and Majestic: "And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them" [al-Nisa': 18], etc.

Some scholars said: They saw the signs of the punishment and repented. This does not prevent it, and what the scholars have said on this has already been mentioned in Surat Yunus [[See vol. 8, p. 384, first or second edition.]], so let it be consulted there.

His words: ﴿or they increase﴾. The meanings of "aw" in His words "aw ashaddu qaswah" have already passed in al-Baqarah [[See vol. 1, pp. 463 ff., second or third edition.]]. Al-Farra' said: "Aw" here means "bal" (rather). Others said: It means "wa" (and), and from this is the poet's saying:

"When the matter of war grew intense among us, and we considered the winds, or the clouds (rizam)."

Meaning: "or [they were] more", and this is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the matter of the Hour is but as a glance of the eye or closer﴾ [16:77]. Ja'far ibn Muhammad read "ila mi'at alf wa-yazidun" without hamza, so "yazidun" is in the place of nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning "and they are increasing." Al-Nahhas said: These two opinions are not sound according to the Basrans. They rejected that "aw" (or) means "bal" (rather) or means "wa" (and), because "bal" is for turning away from the first statement and affirming what follows it, and exalted is Allah, mighty and majestic, above that; or [it is for] moving from one thing to another, and this is not the place for that. The meaning of "wa" is different from the meaning of "aw," so if either of them meant the other, the meanings would be nullified. And if that were permissible, it would be [more concise to say] "wa-arsalnahu ila akthara min mi'atay alf" (and We sent him to more than two hundred thousand).

Al-Mubarrad said: The meaning is "and We sent him to a group which, if you saw them, you would say: they are a hundred thousand or more," and the servants were addressed in terms of what they know. It was said: It is like when you say: "Zayd or 'Amr came to me," while you know which of the two came to you, except that you have made it ambiguous to the addressee. Al-Akhfash and al-Zajjaj said: That is, "or they increase in your estimation."

Ibn 'Abbas said: They exceeded one hundred thousand by twenty thousand. Ubayy ibn Ka'b narrated it as a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ) report. And also from Ibn 'Abbas: thirty thousand. Al-Hasan and al-Rabi': some thirty thousand. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: seventy thousand.

﴿So they believed, and We gave them enjoyment for a time﴾ — that is, until the end of their appointed terms.

**Qur'an 37:149–157**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So ask them: "Does your Lord have daughters while they have sons?"﴾. When He mentioned the reports about earlier peoples, as consolation to the Prophet (ﷺ), He argued against the disbelievers of Quraysh in their claim that the angels are daughters of God, so He said: "So ask them." This is joined to a similar phrase at the beginning of the surah, even though the distance between them is great. That is, "O Muhammad, ask the people of Makkah: 'Does your Lord have daughters?'" This is because Juhaynah, Khuza'ah, Banu Maliḥ, Banu Salamah and 'Abd al-Dar claimed that the angels are daughters of God. This is a question of rebuke.

﴿Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?﴾, that is, present at Our creating them as females. This is like the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And they made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 19]. Then He said: ﴿Unquestionably, it is of their own fabrication [ifk] that they say, "Allah has begotten," and indeed they are liars﴾, in their saying that God has a son, while He is the One who neither begets nor is begotten. The *inna* after *alā* (unquestionably) is with a kasra, because it begins a new sentence. Sibawayh reported that it may come after *amā* with a fatḥa or a kasra. The fatḥa is on the basis that *amā* means *alā*. Al-Nahhas said: "I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: it is permissible to open it after *alā*, by analogy with *amā*. In the verse, however, only the kasra is permissible, because what follows it is in the nominative." The sentence is complete at "liars."

Then a new clause begins: ﴿"Has He chosen daughters over sons?"﴾, in the sense of reproach and rebuke, as if He said: "Woe to you! Has He chosen daughters," that is, preferred daughters and left sons. The common reading is *aṣṭafā* with a cut alif (hamzat al-qaṭʿ), because it is an interrogative alif (*alif al-istifhām*) that entered upon the connecting alif (*alif al-waṣl*). The connecting alif is dropped and the interrogative alif remains, open and cut, in its original state, like *aṭṭalaʿa al-ghayb* (Has he looked into the unseen?), as already discussed [see vol. 11, p. 147, first or second edition]. Abu Jaʿfar, Shaybah, Nafiʿ and Ḥamzah read *iṣṭafā* with a connected alif, as a statement and not as a question. When it begins a sentence, it takes a kasra on the hamza. Abu Ḥatim claimed that there is no justification for this reading, because what follows it is "What is the matter with you? How do you judge?" So the speech continues in rebuke from two aspects. The first is that it is an explanation and clarification of their lie, and "What is the matter with you? How do you judge?" is a separate statement, cut off from what precedes it. The second aspect is that the grammarians, including al-Farrāʾ, reported that rebuke may come with an interrogative and without an interrogative, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿You squandered your good things in your worldly life﴾ [al-Aḥqāf: 20]. It was also said that it is governed by an implied verb of speech, meaning "and they say, 'Has He chosen daughters?'" Or it may be a substitute for His saying "Allah has begotten," because bearing daughters and taking them is choosing them for oneself, so the past form is replaced by the past form. On this view, one does not stop at "they are liars."

﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ That it is impossible for Him to have a son.

﴿Or do you have a clear authority?﴾ A proof and evidence.

﴿Then bring your scripture, if you are truthful.﴾

That is, bring your proofs, if you are truthful in your claim.

**"They have made between Him and the jinn a kinship"** (﴿وَجَعَلُوا بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْجِنَّةِ نَسَباً﴾). Most of the people of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) hold that *al-jinnah* here means the angels. Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid that he said: They, meaning the disbelievers of Quraysh, said: "The angels are the daughters of Allah, exalted is He." Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Then who are their mothers?" They said: "The veiled women of the jinn." The philologists (*ahl al-ishtiqaq*) said: they were called *jinnah* because they are not seen. Mujahid said: they are a clan of the angels called *al-jinnah*, and this is also narrated from Ibn Abbas. Israil narrated from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, who said: They were only called *jinnah* because they are guardians of the gardens (*al-janan*), and all the angels are *jinnah*.

"Kinship" (*nasaban*) means marriage alliance (*musaharah*). Qatada, al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: The Jews, may Allah curse them, said: "Allah has intermarried with the jinn, and so the angels came from among them." Mujahid, al-Suddi and Muqatil also said: those who said this were the tribes of Kinanah and Khuza'ah. They said: "Allah proposed to the chiefs of the jinn and they married Him to the noblest of their daughters, so the angels are the daughters of Allah from the noblest daughters of the jinn." Al-Hasan said: They associated Satan with the worship of Allah, and this is the kinship they invented. I say: al-Hasan's view on this is the best, and its proof is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿when We equated you with the Lord of the worlds﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:98), meaning in worship. Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak and al-Hasan also said: it is their saying that Allah, the Exalted, and Iblis are two brothers. Allah is exalted far above what they say, a great exaltation.

**"But the jinn know that they will indeed be brought forth"** (﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمَتِ الْجِنَّةُ إِنَّهُمْ لَمُحْضَرُونَ﴾). **Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 37, verses 161–163:**

There are three issues (masa'il) in this passage.

**First:** Allah's words, ﴿So indeed you and what you worship﴾. Here "mā" (ما) means "alladhī" (الَّذِي, "that which"). It is also said that it means the verbal noun (al-masdar), so that the meaning is: "indeed you and your worship of these idols." It is also said that the meaning is: "indeed you, together with what you worship besides God," as one says, "So-and-so came, and so-and-so," and "So-and-so came with so-and-so."

﴿Not one of you can lead astray concerning Him﴾: "mā antum 'alayhi" means "concerning God," and "bi-fatinin" means "those who lead astray" (bi-mudilin). Al-Nahhas said: As far as I know, the people of tafsir (exegesis) agree that the meaning is: "You cannot lead anyone astray except those whom God, Mighty and Majestic, has decreed to go astray." The poet said:

*So He turned back his plot with His favour,*
*and against him, and He was for us a tempter (fatinan),*

that is, a misleader (mudillan).

**Second:** In this verse there is a refutation of the Qadariyya (those who deny divine predestination). ʿAmr ibn Dharr said: "We came to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzIz, and predestination (al-qadar) was mentioned in his presence. ʿUmar said: 'If God had willed that He not be disobeyed, He would not have created Iblis, who is the head of sin. There is knowledge of this in the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic; whoever knows it knows it, and whoever is ignorant of it is ignorant. Then he recited: ﴿So indeed you and what you worship, you cannot lead astray concerning Him, except him who is destined by God, Mighty and Majestic, to burn in the Blazing Fire.﴾'" He also said: "This verse distinguishes between people, and among its meanings is that the devils cannot reach the misguidance of anyone except him whom God has decreed will not be guided. Had God, Mighty and Majestic, known that he would be guided, He would have come between him and them." On this basis is the words of God, the Exalted: ﴿And incite against them with your cavalry and your infantry﴾ [al-Isra' 17:64], meaning: you will not reach anything from them except what is within My knowledge.

Labid ibn Rabi'a said, affirming predestination, and he did well:

*Indeed, the piety of our Lord is the best provision,*
*and by God's permission my delay and my haste are His.*

*I praise God, for there is no equal to Him,*
*and in His hands is the good; He does whatever He wills.*

*Whom He guides to the paths of goodness is guided,*
*and is at ease of heart; and whom He wills He leads astray.*

Al-Farra' said: "The people of the Hijaz say *fatantu al-rajul* (I tempted the man), and the people of Najd say *aftantuhu*."

**Third:** It is narrated from al-Hasan that he recited ﴿except him who is ṣālu al-Jaḥīm (صَالُ الْجَحِيمِ)﴾ with a *ḍamma* on the *lām*. Al-Nahhas said: "The community of the people of tafsir say that this is a lahn (grammatical error), because it is not permissible." The judge of Madina said: Among the best of what has been said about it is what I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulayman say: he said, "It is understood according to the meaning, because the meaning of *man* (مَنْ) is a group (jamāʿa), so the underlying form is ṣālūna (صَالُونَ), the *nūn* was dropped for the construct (idafa), and the *wāw* was dropped because two unvocalized letters came together."

It is also said that its origin is *fāʿil* (فَاعِلٌ), except that it was changed from *ṣāl* to *ṣā'il* (صائل), the *yā'* was dropped, and the *lām* remained *ḍamma*-vocalized. This is like ﴿on the brink of a crumbling precipice﴾ [al-Tawba 9:109] (شَفا جُرُفٍ هارٍ).

A third explanation is that the final letter (*lām*) of *ṣāl* is dropped for lightness, and the inflection (iʿrab) is applied to its middle letter, just as it was dropped in their saying, *mā bālaytu bihi bālatan* (I did not care about it at all). Its origin is *bāliyatun* from *bāli*, like *ʿāfiyatun* from *ʿāfi*. A parallel to this is the reading of whoever read ﴿and the fruit of the two gardens is near﴾ [al-Rahman 55:54] and ﴿and His are the ships, raised high﴾ [al-Rahman 55:24], where the inflection was applied to the middle letter. The original form in the reading of the community is *ṣāliy* with a *yā'*, which the scribe dropped from the written text because it is dropped in pronunciation.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 37, verses 161–163:**

There are three issues (masa'il) in this passage.

**First:** Allah's words, ﴿So indeed you and what you worship﴾. Here "mā" (ما) means "alladhī" (الَّذِي, "that which"). It is also said that it means the verbal noun (al-masdar), so that the meaning is: "indeed you and your worship of these idols." It is also said that the meaning is: "indeed you, together with what you worship besides God," as one says, "So-and-so came, and so-and-so," and "So-and-so came with so-and-so."

﴿Not one of you can lead astray concerning Him﴾: "mā antum 'alayhi" means "concerning God," and "bi-fatinin" means "those who lead astray" (bi-mudilin). Al-Nahhas said: As far as I know, the people of tafsir (exegesis) agree that the meaning is: "You cannot lead anyone astray except those whom God, Mighty and Majestic, has decreed to go astray." The poet said:

*So He turned back his plot with His favour,*
*and against him, and He was for us a tempter (fatinan),*

that is, a misleader (mudillan).

**Second:** In this verse there is a refutation of the Qadariyya (those who deny divine predestination). ʿAmr ibn Dharr said: "We came to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzIz, and predestination (al-qadar) was mentioned in his presence. ʿUmar said: 'If God had willed that He not be disobeyed, He would not have created Iblis, who is the head of sin. There is knowledge of this in the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic; whoever knows it knows it, and whoever is ignorant of it is ignorant. Then he recited: ﴿So indeed you and what you worship, you cannot lead astray concerning Him, except him who is destined by God, Mighty and Majestic, to burn in the Blazing Fire.﴾'" He also said: "This verse distinguishes between people, and among its meanings is that the devils cannot reach the misguidance of anyone except him whom God has decreed will not be guided. Had God, Mighty and Majestic, known that he would be guided, He would have come between him and them." On this basis is the words of God, the Exalted: ﴿And incite against them with your cavalry and your infantry﴾ [al-Isra' 17:64], meaning: you will not reach anything from them except what is within My knowledge.

Labid ibn Rabi'a said, affirming predestination, and he did well:

*Indeed, the piety of our Lord is the best provision,*
*and by God's permission my delay and my haste are His.*

*I praise God, for there is no equal to Him,*
*and in His hands is the good; He does whatever He wills.*

*Whom He guides to the paths of goodness is guided,*
*and is at ease of heart; and whom He wills He leads astray.*

Al-Farra' said: "The people of the Hijaz say *fatantu al-rajul* (I tempted the man), and the people of Najd say *aftantuhu*."
